apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — CRITICAL auth bypass: `req.headers[name] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, an anonymous request with no header gives `undefined !== undefined` = false, so the check passes and any caller can write credentials.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34-92 — CRITICAL IDOR: `userId` is taken verbatim from the body and used to update/create a credential for ANY user in the instance. One leaked secret = tenant-wide OAuth credential takeover. No rate limiting, no audit record.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:32-45 — HIGH privilege escalation: the team branch checks only `members.some({userId, accepted: true})` with no ADMIN/OWNER role filter, then creates a team-scoped credential. Any accepted plain member can attach an app credential to the whole team.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId})` sits AFTER the `if (state?.teamId) {...return}` block, so it is only reachable when teamId is falsy and is always called with `teamId: null`. The admin gate is unreachable dead code that reads like protection.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` but `prisma` is never imported in this file (verified: imports are jsforce/rrule/zod/@calcom/lib/*/@calcom/types/*/getAppKeysFromSlug/parseRefreshTokenResponse). ReferenceError / compile break.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` returns the zod safeParse WRAPPER, not `.data`; it is written straight to `credential.key`, storing `{success: true, data: {...}}`. The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` which returned the payload. Bricks every Google credential on refresh — and this fires with the feature DISABLED.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8-10 — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, so the object collapses to `{access_token, "[object Object]"?}`. "Any numeric property is the expiry" and "allow other properties" are not implemented; z.object strips unknowns, so in sync mode `.data` contains ONLY access_token — expiry and refresh fields are silently discarded before being persisted.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — the `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` sentinel write is NOT gated on sync mode. At office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264, `refresh_token` is optional in the schema and MS often omits it, so `{...creds, ...tokenResponse.data}` overwrites the real refresh token with the literal string `"refresh_token"` — permanent credential poisoning on the default path.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19 — core design defect: the sync branch returns a raw `fetch` Response, the fallback returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns. No common type, no discriminant, and `refreshFunction: () => any` erases the mismatch so all call sites type-check while several break at runtime.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-94 — sync branch returns a Response (no `.data`), but the code reads `res?.data` then `token.access_token` → TypeError. Google refresh is dead in sync mode.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-202 — same mismatch; `: HubspotToken` annotation is a lie over `any`. `expiresIn` undefined → `expiryDate = NaN`, the whole Response object is persisted as `credential.key`, and `setAccessToken(undefined)`. The surrounding try/catch swallows it, so refresh silently no-ops.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95 — sync Response is fed to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>`, which expects Lark's `{code, msg, data:{...}}` envelope; a flat sync response yields `data.data` undefined → TypeError. Lark never calls parseRefreshTokenResponse.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:62-89 — converted to refreshOAuthTokens but NOT to parseRefreshTokenResponse, so the sync response is validated against the strict `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` (requires refresh_token, refresh_token_expires_in, a z.literal scope) and always fails.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:61-93 — skips parseRefreshTokenResponse and overwrites the ENTIRE `credential.key` with `responseBody` (verified at line 93). A sync endpoint returning only `{access_token, expires_in}` permanently erases the stored refresh_token — unrecoverable.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/{refreshOAuthTokens.ts:1, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:3}, apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:5 — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is imported from @calcom/lib/constants but the diff never defines it and never touches packages/lib/constants.ts. If it is genuinely absent upstream, every sync branch is dead and the webhook always 403s. (Cannot be fully confirmed — constants.ts is outside this snapshot.)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 — HIGH: `symmetricDecrypt(keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`. The `|| ""` fallback silently accepts a misconfigured deployment, and Cal.com's symmetricDecrypt is AES-256-CBC with no MAC — the ciphertext is unauthenticated and malleable, so decryption is not an authentication boundary behind the header check.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — HIGH: `JSON.parse` of decrypted bytes with no try/catch and no schema; the result is written directly into `credential.key` (lines 78, 84). Arbitrary JSON — including access_token/refresh_token pointing at attacker infrastructure — is persisted unvalidated.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — MEDIUM: timing-unsafe secret comparison (`!==` instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual); also no guard for array-valued headers, and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is used verbatim while Node lowercases incoming header names (only a comment in .env.example warns about this).
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — MEDIUM: no HTTP method restriction; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the mutation path, with no origin/Content-Type check.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — MEDIUM: `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` on attacker-controlled input with no try/catch (unhandled SyntaxError → 500 on every OAuth callback) and no schema — the `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` annotation is an unchecked cast, and `state.teamId` flows unvalidated into prisma queries and `credential.create`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — MEDIUM: the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries NO authentication (no bearer, no signature, no shared secret) while transmitting calcomUserId, and there is no `response.ok` check — a 4xx/5xx body is returned as if it were tokens and written into credential.key.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — MEDIUM: the hardcoded `"refresh_token"` sentinel is persisted as a real credential value and later sent to the provider; it also makes "has a refresh token" checks pass falsely, masking broken credentials instead of forcing re-auth.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:38-47 — LOW: distinct 404 bodies ("User not found" vs "App not found") plus success messages echoing userId allow user/app enumeration once past the secret check.
Completeness / error handling**
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `.parse` (not safeParse), unguarded: a malformed body throws ZodError out of the handler → 500 with detail instead of 400.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-90 — only user credentials are supported; team credentials (teamId set, userId null — which createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47-54 creates) are invisible to sync, and the request schema has no way to express a team target.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-70 — the update path never clears the `invalid` flag, so a previously-invalidated credential stays flagged after a successful sync and the fresh key is ignored.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 — the function throws on failure but returns a SafeParseReturnType, so callers' `.success` checks are dead code: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 and salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92. Pick one contract.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-265 — in sync mode `.data` is `{access_token}` only, so expires_in is never updated; `isExpired()` stays true and every request triggers a fresh refresh (unbounded amplification against the sync endpoint).

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:248-255 — the zod-failure `console.error` (zodError + raw MS response) was deleted with no replacement; Outlook token-parse debugging is gone.

repo-wide — no tests added for the webhook handler, parseRefreshTokenResponse, or refreshOAuthTokens; no validation evidence for the sync path in any of the 8 apps (corroborates the deterministic validation gate).
.env.example:233-243 — the env var backing APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (the master switch for the entire feature) is documented nowhere, though the four secondary vars are.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-90 — check-then-insert TOCTOU: findFirst-then-create with no unique constraint, no upsert, no transaction. Two concurrent webhooks for the same (userId, appId) both miss and both create duplicates. No idempotency key, so a retried delivery is indistinguishable from a new one.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-70 — `findFirst` with no orderBy and no uniqueness guarantee: once duplicates exist, which credential gets updated is nondeterministic and the stale sibling keeps being served.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:41-46 — `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app dirName (e.g. `googlecalendar`), but the code indexes it with `app.slug` from the DB (e.g. `google-calendar`); hyphenated apps would 404. Unconfirmed — appStoreMetaData.ts is outside this snapshot.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — ~28 lines of new unconditional token-refresh + credential.update added to getClient. This is new functionality, not required by credential sync, and it notably does NOT route through refreshOAuthTokens — it bypasses the very indirection this PR adds.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — the refresh runs on EVERY getClient() call with no expiry check, and the freshly fetched token is never used: the jsforce.Connection below is still built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`, making the added refresh pointless.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (undici/HTTP-2 commonly return an empty statusText); should be `!response.ok`. Can throw on every successful refresh, or let an error response fall through to be persisted.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — unrelated change replacing `${appConfig.slug}` with a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` in the redirect URI. Pure churn, a regression in config-driven behavior, and inconsistent with lines 12 and 22 which still use appConfig.slug.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 vs decodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 — byte-identical logic; encodeOAuthState is JSON.parse followed by JSON.stringify, a no-op round trip that encodes nothing. Two files, one behavior, misleading names.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 and parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` duplicated verbatim in two modules that must agree; drift makes refresh fail opaquely. Belongs behind one exported predicate.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5,8 — mixed evaluation timing for one logical flag (module-scope constant + per-request process.env read), and the endpoint URL is never validated at boot, so a typo surfaces only at token-refresh time in production.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — the appSlug is a free-form string literal per call site ("google-calendar", "msteams", "office365-calendar", "lark-calendar", "webex", "hubspot") rather than derived from app metadata, so it can silently diverge from the appSlug the webhook expects on the way back in.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `select: { members: { select: { userId: true } } }` is fetched and never used.

Not reported: the `.env.example` EOF-newline fix (trivial), and the `-base64 24` vs "32 bytes" comment (24 random bytes base64-encodes to the 32-character key string `symmetricDecrypt` expects, so it is correct as written).

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34-92 — CRITICAL IDOR: `userId` is taken verbatim from the body and used to update/create a credential for ANY user in the instance. One leaked secret = tenant-wide OAuth credential takeover. No rate limiting, no audit record.

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes requests solely by checking a static shared secret header (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). After that, it trusts `reqBody.userId` from the request body and performs `prisma.credential.update/create` for that user’s credentials with no further scoping/authorization tying the caller to that specific user. Therefore, anyone who can send requests with the shared secret can update/create credentials for arbitrary users by choosing any `userId` (tenant-wide impact if the secret is leaked/abused). The diff also shows no rate limiting or audit logging around these mutations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` returns the zod safeParse WRAPPER, not `.data`; it is written straight to `credential.key`, storing `{success: true, data: {...}}`. The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` which returned the payload. Bricks every Google credential on refresh — and this fires with the feature DISABLED.
matched_golden_ids: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same core bug: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result wrapper (`{ success, data, error }`), but the code persists that wrapper directly into `credential.key` instead of using `.data` (or using `schema.parse()` to get the payload). This matches the golden comment’s concern about storing the wrapper rather than the token payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8-10 — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, so the object collapses to `{access_token, "[object Object]"?}`. "Any numeric property is the expiry" and "allow other properties" are not implemented; z.object strips unknowns, so in sync mode `.data` contains ONLY access_token — expiry and refresh fields are silently discarded before being persisted.
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: using computed property keys derived from `z.string().toString()` / `z.string().optional().toString()` is incorrect and results in an unintended key ("[object Object]") rather than valid dynamic keys. While the golden comment emphasizes a runtime error/invalid Zod syntax, the candidate explains the concrete failure mode (schema collapsing/stripping), which stems from the same misuse of computed keys in the Zod object schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — the `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` sentinel write is NOT gated on sync mode. At office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264, `refresh_token` is optional in the schema and MS often omits it, so `{...creds, ...tokenResponse.data}` overwrites the real refresh token with the literal string `"refresh_token"` — permanent credential poisoning on the default path.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: when the OAuth refresh token response omits `refresh_token` (common with Microsoft), the code assigns the literal string "refresh_token" and merges it into stored credentials, overwriting/poisoning the real refresh token and causing future refresh/auth failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19 — core design defect: the sync branch returns a raw `fetch` Response, the fallback returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns. No common type, no discriminant, and `refreshFunction: () => any` erases the mismatch so all call sites type-check while several break at runtime.
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: in the sync-enabled branch the helper returns a raw fetch Response, while callers expect an integration-specific token object (e.g., res.data / HubspotToken). The candidate also notes the lack of a common return type and that `any` hides the mismatch at compile time, leading to runtime failures, which aligns with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-94 — sync branch returns a Response (no `.data`), but the code reads `res?.data` then `token.access_token` → TypeError. Google refresh is dead in sync mode.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch(...)` Response when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true. A `Response` object does not have a `.data` property, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime in sync mode. The non-sync branch still returns `fetchTokens.res` from `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken`, which likely has `.data`, highlighting the inconsistency introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-202 — same mismatch; `: HubspotToken` annotation is a lie over `any`. `expiresIn` undefined → `expiryDate = NaN`, the whole Response object is persisted as `credential.key`, and `setAccessToken(undefined)`. adjudication.rationale: The diff changes HubSpot token refresh to call `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and assigns the result to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = ...`. However, `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in the diff) returns a `fetch(...)` **Response** object (not parsed JSON / not a HubspotToken shape) when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true. The core mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff; the finding’s extra details about exactly what gets persisted are more speculative, but the underlying bug is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95 — sync Response is fed to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>`, which expects Lark's `{code, msg, data:{...}}` envelope; a flat sync response yields `data.data` undefined → TypeError. Lark never calls parseRefreshTokenResponse.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh token flow now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then unconditionally passes the returned `resp` into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` will, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && credential.userId`, return the HTTP `Response` from the *sync endpoint* (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), whose inline comment explicitly says the response “should only contain the access token and expiry date” (i.e., not Lark’s `{ code, msg, data: {...} }` envelope). That means in the sync-enabled path, `handleLarkError` is very likely to parse/validate a Lark-shaped body and then downstream code will not find the expected nested `data` fields, causing runtime failure (at minimum incorrect parsing; plausibly `undefined` access). Unlike Google/Office365/Salesforce, Lark refresh does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to tolerate a minimal token response, so the mismatch is introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 — HIGH: `symmetricDecrypt(keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`. The `|| ""` fallback silently accepts a misconfigured deployment, and Cal.com's symmetricDecrypt is AES-256-CBC with no MAC — the ciphertext is unauthenticated and malleable, so decryption is not an authentication boundary behind the header check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, meaning a missing `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` will fall back to an empty string instead of failing fast. That is a verifiable misconfiguration footgun and can turn decryption into a potentially weaker/undefined operation rather than rejecting the request. However, the claim that Cal.com’s `symmetricDecrypt` is specifically “AES-256-CBC with no MAC” is not verifiable from this diff alone (it depends on implementation outside the change).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — HIGH: `JSON.parse` of decrypted bytes with no try/catch and no schema; the result is written directly into `credential.key` (lines 78, 84). Arbitrary JSON — including access_token/refresh_token pointing at attacker infrastructure — is persisted unvalidated.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` and immediately does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` with no try/catch. If the decrypted string is not valid JSON, the handler will throw and return a 500 (unhandled exception). Additionally, the parsed `keys` object is not validated against any schema before being persisted to the database as `credential.key` in both the update and create paths (`data: { key: keys }`). While the endpoint is guarded by a shared-secret header, the diff does introduce an unvalidated arbitrary-JSON persistence path as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — MEDIUM: timing-unsafe secret comparison (`!==` instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual); also no guard for array-valued headers, and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is used verbatim while Node lowercases incoming header names (only a comment in .env.example warns about this).

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does a direct `!==` comparison between `req.headers[headerName]` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next/Node, `req.headers[...]` is typed/behaves as `string | string[] | undefined`, so an array-valued header (or missing header) will never equal the secret and is not explicitly handled. Also, the lookup key is taken verbatim from `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`; Node normalizes incoming header names to lowercase in `req.headers`, so if an operator configures a mixed/upper-case name the lookup will fail (the .env comment warns about this, but the code doesn’t enforce/normalize it). The timing-safe comparison point is also grounded: the code uses ordinary equality instead of a constant-time compare for a secret check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — MEDIUM: no HTTP method restriction; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the mutation path, with no origin/Content-Type check.

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` exports a `handler(req, res)` that performs auth checks and then immediately `parse`s `req.body` and runs Prisma `update`/`create` mutations, but it never checks `req.method` (e.g., `if (req.method !== 'POST') ...`). As written, any HTTP method (PUT/DELETE/etc.) that can carry a body and includes the correct webhook secret header will execute the same mutation logic. There is also no Content-Type/origin validation in this handler. This is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — MEDIUM: the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries NO authentication (no bearer, no signature, no shared secret) while transmitting calcomUserId, and there is no `response.ok` check — a 4xx/5xx body is returned as if it were tokens and written into credential.key.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the branch that calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` does not add any authentication (no shared-secret header, bearer token, signature, etc.) and does not check `response.ok` before returning the `Response` object. That is directly verifiable in lines 8–14. However, the finding’s claim that a 4xx/5xx body is then “written into credential.key” is not strictly shown by this diff: callers often parse/validate and may throw, and in some cases (e.g., GoogleCalendar) they incorrectly assume an axios-like `{data}` shape and would likely crash rather than write the error. Still, the lack of authentication and lack of HTTP status handling in `refreshOAuthTokens` is a real issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — MEDIUM: the hardcoded `"refresh_token"` sentinel is persisted as a real credential value and later sent to the provider; it also makes "has a refresh token" checks pass falsely, masking broken credentials instead of forcing re-auth.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:38-47 — LOW: distinct 404 bodies ("User not found" vs "App not found") plus success messages echoing userId allow user/app enumeration once past the secret check.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler returns distinguishable responses based on existence checks: 404 with {message:"User not found"} when prisma.user.findUnique() fails, 404 with {message:"App not found"} when prisma.app.findUnique() fails, and a different 404 message when appStoreMetadata lookup fails. It also returns 200 responses whose message strings include the provided userId ("Credentials updated/created for userId: X"). Therefore, for any caller who can satisfy the shared-secret header check, the endpoint’s responses can be used to confirm whether a given userId exists and whether a given appSlug is valid, i.e., enumeration/information disclosure as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 — the function throws on failure but returns a SafeParseReturnType, so callers' `.success` checks are dead code: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 and salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92. Pick one contract.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function uses `schema.safeParse(...)` (returning a `SafeParseReturnType`) but then immediately throws if `!refreshTokenResponse.success`. That means any successful return is guaranteed to have `success === true`, making downstream `.success` checks redundant/dead code. This is directly visible in the diff in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` where it does `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` after calling `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`; that condition can never be false unless an exception was thrown earlier. The finding’s “pick one contract” critique (either return parsed data or return a SafeParse result without throwing) is valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-90 — check-then-insert TOCTOU: findFirst-then-create with no unique constraint, no upsert, no transaction. Two concurrent webhooks for the same (userId, appId) both miss and both create duplicates. No idempotency key, so a retried delivery is indistinguishable from a new one.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler does a non-atomic existence check (`prisma.credential.findFirst` on `{ userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }`) and then conditionally `create` if none is found. This is a classic TOCTOU race: two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both observe “no credential” and both execute `prisma.credential.create`, resulting in duplicate rows if the DB doesn’t enforce a unique constraint, or a unique-violation error if it does. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-70 — `findFirst` with no orderBy and no uniqueness guarantee: once duplicates exist, which credential gets updated is nondeterministic and the stale sibling keeps being served.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the code uses prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } }) with no orderBy, then updates only the returned record. The code comment explicitly says it "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential", which strongly implies there is no unique constraint on (userId, appId) to safely upsert by a unique key. In that situation, duplicates are possible (e.g., from past data or concurrent webhook requests), and findFirst without an orderBy is nondeterministic, so the handler may update an arbitrary duplicate while leaving another stale credential in place.
